answer: 514 genes. Using DESeq2 (design ~ Media + Strain) relative to JBX1 (= reference strain code '1', not explicitly labeled) with BH FDR padj < 0.05, 514 genes are uniquely and significantly differentially expressed in at least one of the ΔlasI/ΔrhlI single mutants (strain codes 97/98) but not in the ΔlasIΔrhlI double mutant (code 99, adopted as the double because it shows the most DE genes). Per-contrast DE vs JBX1: 97=2549, 98=3069, 99=4072; unique = |DE97 ∪ DE98| − |(DE97 ∪ DE98) ∩ DE99| = 3840 − 3326 = 514. Caveats: the double-mutant identity is not derivable from the files — if code 98 were the double the count is 1517, if code 97 then 2037; the DESeq2 dispersion-shrinkage prior weight gives 424–536. R/DESeq2 was unavailable in the offline environment, so a faithful DESeq2-equivalent (median-of-ratios size factors + NB GLM + dispersion trend/MAP + Wald + BH) was executed.
